A closed mountain observatory operations desk applies exact telescope dome rules. Use only the listed dossier records and provisions.
Closed-dossier note: an entry's status holds only when listed under Observed Statuses, derived via Decision Provisions, or reported in a verified telemetry bulletin.

Observed Statuses:
Entry 1: Telescope Optic-68 is registered under active default status.
Entry 2: Telescope Optic-68 belongs to Bay Nadir.
Entry 3: Telescope Optic-29 belongs to Bay Zenith.
Entry 4: For Telescope Optic-68, the shutter bolt is released.
Entry 5: Telescope Optic-47 passed collimation sweep.
Entry 6: Telescope Optic-14 verified dew heater check.

Clause 1 — For entries in Bay Nadir, if Telescope Optic-68 logged a tracking shift, then Telescope Optic-68 enters mirror calibration.
Clause 2 — When Telescope Optic-68 confirmed thermal equilibrium, it follows that Telescope Optic-68 clears night priority.
Clause 3 — When Telescope Optic-68 enters mirror calibration and Telescope Optic-68 clears night priority, it follows that Telescope Optic-68 authorizes dome override.
Clause 4 — When Telescope Optic-68 authorizes dome override, supersede the baseline assignment and route Telescope Optic-68 to Dome-Rigel.
Clause 5 — When Telescope Optic-68 logged a tracking shift and Telescope Optic-68 enters mirror calibration, it follows that Telescope Optic-68 holds a focus bulletin.
Clause 6 — When Telescope Optic-68 holds a focus bulletin and Telescope Optic-68 carries an emergency board waiver, supersede the baseline assignment and route Telescope Optic-68 to Dome-Vega.
Clause 7 — If Telescope Optic-47 passed collimation sweep and Telescope Optic-14 verified dew heater check, record a routine audit note for Telescope Optic-47.
Clause 8 — When Telescope Optic-29 logged a tracking shift, it follows that Telescope Optic-29 is placed on a standby list.

Baseline Rule: Telescope Optic-68 is under active default status, so Telescope Optic-68 is assigned to Dome-Lyra unless the rules establish that Telescope Optic-68 authorizes dome override.

Question: Based strictly on the listed dossier entries and provisions, what is the current classification of Telescope Optic-68?

context_prompt_v:
[Operations Memo]
A closed geothermal seismic monitoring station applies exact telemetry rules. Use only the listed dossier records and provisions.
Closed-memo note: a status holds only if stated under Current Records, derived from Operating Directives, or supplied in a verified field update.

Current Records:
Record #1: Sensor Node-78 is registered under active default status.
Record #2: Sensor Node-78 belongs to Ridge Crest.
Record #3: Sensor Node-17 belongs to Ridge Trough.
Record #4: For Sensor Node-78, the tremor gate is released.
Record #5: Sensor Node-35 passed geophone ping.
Record #6: Sensor Node-53 verified battery voltage.

Standing Rule: Sensor Node-78 is under active default status, so Sensor Node-78 is assigned to Band-Wave unless the rules establish that Sensor Node-78 triggers borehole override.

Operating Directives:
Directive 1: For entries in Ridge Crest, if Sensor Node-78 emitted a p-wave chime, then Sensor Node-78 enters waveform triage.
Directive 2: In cases where Sensor Node-78 confirmed borehole telemetry sync, establish that Sensor Node-78 enables array priority.
Directive 3: In cases where Sensor Node-78 enters waveform triage and Sensor Node-78 enables array priority, establish that Sensor Node-78 triggers borehole override.
Directive 4: In cases where Sensor Node-78 triggers borehole override, replace the standing assignment and direct Sensor Node-78 to Band-Drift.
Directive 5: In cases where Sensor Node-78 emitted a p-wave chime and Sensor Node-78 enters waveform triage, establish that Sensor Node-78 carries a spectrum log.
Directive 6: In cases where Sensor Node-78 carries a spectrum log and Sensor Node-78 carries an emergency board waiver, replace the standing assignment and direct Sensor Node-78 to Band-Echo.
Directive 7: If Sensor Node-35 passed geophone ping and Sensor Node-53 verified battery voltage, record a routine audit note for Sensor Node-35.
Directive 8: In cases where Sensor Node-17 emitted a p-wave chime, establish that Sensor Node-17 is placed on a standby list.

Question: Using only the current records and operating directives above, what is the assigned classification of Sensor Node-78?
Options:
A. Band-Echo
B. Band-Pulse
C. Band-Drift
D. Band-Wave

Directive 8: In cases where Breaker Bus-24 reported a harmonic surge, establish that Breaker Bus-24 is placed on a standby list.

Clause 7 — If Breaker Bus-24 passed oil dielectric test and Breaker Bus-52 logged grounding continuity, record a routine audit note for Breaker Bus-24.
Clause 8 — When Breaker Bus-38 reported a harmonic surge, it follows that Breaker Bus-38 is placed on a standby list.

Question: Based strictly on the listed dossier entries and provisions, what is the current classification of Breaker Bus-11?
Options:
A. Tap-Amber

[Operations Memo]
A closed high-voltage substation desk enforces exact feeder rules. Use only the listed dossier records and provisions.
Closed-memo note: a status holds only if stated under Current Records, derived from Operating Directives, or supplied in a verified field update.

Current Records:
Record #1: Breaker Bus-24 is registered under active default status.
Record #2: For Breaker Bus-24, the arc relay is released.
Record #3: Breaker Bus-52 belongs to Wing Primary.
Record #4: Breaker Bus-38 passed oil dielectric test.
Record #5: Breaker Bus-11 logged grounding continuity.

Operating Directives:
Directive 1: For entries in Wing Reserve, if Breaker Bus-24 reported a harmonic surge, then Breaker Bus-24 enters load balancing.
Directive 2: In cases where Breaker Bus-24 recorded frequency lock, establish that Breaker Bus-24 opens voltage priority.
Directive 3: In cases where Breaker Bus-24 enters load balancing and Breaker Bus-24 opens voltage priority, establish that Breaker Bus-24 activates busbar override.
Directive 4: In cases where Breaker Bus-24 activates busbar override, replace the standing assignment and direct Breaker Bus-24 to Tap-Slate.
Directive 5: In cases where Breaker Bus-24 reported a harmonic surge and Breaker Bus-24 enters load balancing, establish that Breaker Bus-24 carries a transformer notice.
Directive 6: In cases where Breaker Bus-24 carries a transformer notice and Breaker Bus-24 carries an emergency board waiver, replace the standing assignment and direct Breaker Bus-24 to Tap-Coral.
Directive 7: If Breaker Bus-38 passed oil dielectric test and Breaker Bus-11 logged grounding continuity, record a routine audit note for Breaker Bus-38.
Directive 8: In cases where Breaker Bus-52 reported a harmonic surge, establish that Breaker Bus-52 is placed on a standby list.

Standing Rule: Breaker Bus-24 is under active default status, so Breaker Bus-24 is assigned to Tap-Amber unless the rules establish that Breaker Bus-24 activates busbar override.

Question: Using only the current records and operating directives above, what is the assigned classification of Breaker Bus-24?
Options:
A. Tap-Ivory
B. Tap-Slate
C. Tap-Coral
D. Tap-Amber

Directive 7: If Breaker Bus-11 passed oil dielectric test and Breaker Bus-38 logged grounding continuity, record a routine audit note for Breaker Bus-11.
Directive 8: In cases where Breaker Bus-24 reported a harmonic surge, establish that Breaker Bus-24 is placed on a standby list.

Question: Using only the current records and operating directives above, what is the assigned classification of Breaker Bus-52?

A closed geothermal seismic monitoring station applies exact telemetry rules. Use only the listed dossier records and provisions.

Record #1: Sensor Node-53 is registered under active default status.
Record #2: For Sensor Node-53, the tremor gate is released.
Record #3: Sensor Node-35 belongs to Ridge Crest.
Record #4: Sensor Node-17 passed geophone ping.
Record #5: Sensor Node-78 verified battery voltage.

Operating Directives:
Directive 1: In cases where Sensor Node-53 emitted a p-wave chime, establish that Sensor Node-53 enters waveform triage.
Directive 2: For entries in Ridge Trough, if Sensor Node-53 confirmed borehole telemetry sync, then Sensor Node-53 enables array priority.
Directive 3: In cases where Sensor Node-53 enters waveform triage and Sensor Node-53 enables array priority, establish that Sensor Node-53 triggers borehole override.

Directive 6: In cases where Sensor Node-53 carries a spectrum log and Sensor Node-53 carries an emergency board waiver, replace the standing assignment and direct Sensor Node-53 to Band-Echo.
Directive 7: If Sensor Node-17 passed geophone ping and Sensor Node-78 verified battery voltage, record a routine audit note for Sensor Node-17.
Directive 8: In cases where Sensor Node-35 emitted a p-wave chime, establish that Sensor Node-35 is placed on a standby list.

Standing Rule: Sensor Node-53 is under active default status, so Sensor Node-53 is assigned to Band-Pulse unless the rules establish that Sensor Node-53 triggers borehole override.

Question: Using only the current records and operating directives above, what is the assigned classification of Sensor Node-53?
Options:
A. Band-Drift
B. Band-Pulse
C. Band-Wave
D. Band-Echo

Directive 8: In cases where Sensor Node-35 emitted a p-wave chime, establish that Sensor Node-35 is placed on a standby list.

A closed oceanographic buoy control room applies exact mooring rules. Use only the listed dossier records and provisions.
Closed-memo note: a status holds only if stated under Current Records, derived from Operating Directives, or supplied in a verified field update.

Current Records:
Record #1: Beacon Float-43 is registered under active default status.
Record #2: Beacon Float-43 belongs to Tide Outer.
Record #3: Beacon Float-43 carries a hydrographer tag.
Record #4: For Beacon Float-43, the anchor clip is released.
Record #5: Beacon Float-64 cleared solar panel check.
Record #6: Beacon Float-85 logged transponder sync.

Directive 5: In cases where Beacon Float-43 sent a drift beacon and Beacon Float-43 enters sonar validation, establish that Beacon Float-43 holds a current digest.
Directive 6: In cases where Beacon Float-43 holds a current digest and Beacon Float-43 carries an emergency board waiver, replace the standing assignment and direct Beacon Float-43 to Channel-Plover.
Directive 7: If Beacon Float-64 cleared solar panel check and Beacon Float-85 logged transponder sync, record a routine audit note for Beacon Float-64.
Directive 8: In cases where Beacon Float-21 sent a drift beacon, establish that Beacon Float-21 is placed on a standby list.

Standing Rule: Beacon Float-43 is under active default status, so Beacon Float-43 is assigned to Channel-Heron unless the rules establish that Beacon Float-43 authorizes mooring override.

Question: Using only the current records and operating directives above, what is the assigned classification of Beacon Float-43?

Clause 7 — If Telescope Optic-29 passed collimation sweep and Telescope Optic-68 verified dew heater check, record a routine audit note for Telescope Optic-29.
Clause 8 — When Telescope Optic-14 logged a tracking shift, it follows that Telescope Optic-14 is placed on a standby list.

Directive 7: If Telescope Optic-29 passed collimation sweep and Telescope Optic-47 verified dew heater check, record a routine audit note for Telescope Optic-29.
Directive 8: In cases where Telescope Optic-68 logged a tracking shift, establish that Telescope Optic-68 is placed on a standby list.

context_prompt_v:
[Case Dossier]
A closed high-voltage substation desk enforces exact feeder rules. Use only the listed dossier records and provisions.
Closed-dossier note: an entry's status holds only when listed under Observed Statuses, derived via Decision Provisions, or reported in a verified telemetry bulletin.

Observed Statuses:
Entry 1: Breaker Bus-52 is registered under active default status.
Entry 2: Breaker Bus-52 belongs to Wing Primary.
Entry 3: Breaker Bus-52 holds a dispatcher seal.
Entry 4: For Breaker Bus-52, the arc relay is released.
Entry 5: Breaker Bus-24 passed oil dielectric test.
Entry 6: Breaker Bus-11 logged grounding continuity.

Decision Provisions:
Clause 1 — When Breaker Bus-52 reported a harmonic surge, it follows that Breaker Bus-52 enters load balancing.
Clause 2 — When Breaker Bus-52 recorded frequency lock, it follows that Breaker Bus-52 opens voltage priority.
Clause 3 — When Breaker Bus-52 enters load balancing and Breaker Bus-52 opens voltage priority and Breaker Bus-52 holds a dispatcher seal, it follows that Breaker Bus-52 activates busbar override.
Clause 4 — When Breaker Bus-52 activates busbar override, supersede the baseline assignment and route Breaker Bus-52 to Tap-Coral.
Clause 5 — When Breaker Bus-52 reported a harmonic surge and Breaker Bus-52 enters load balancing, it follows that Breaker Bus-52 carries a transformer notice.
Clause 6 — When Breaker Bus-52 carries a transformer notice and Breaker Bus-52 carries an emergency board waiver, supersede the baseline assignment and route Breaker Bus-52 to Tap-Ivory.
Clause 7 — If Breaker Bus-24 passed oil dielectric test and Breaker Bus-11 logged grounding continuity, record a routine audit note for Breaker Bus-24.
Clause 8 — When Breaker Bus-38 reported a harmonic surge, it follows that Breaker Bus-38 is placed on a standby list.

Baseline Rule: Breaker Bus-52 is under active default status, so Breaker Bus-52 is assigned to Tap-Amber unless the rules establish that Breaker Bus-52 activates busbar override.

Question: Based strictly on the listed dossier entries and provisions, what is the current classification of Breaker Bus-52?
Options:
A. Tap-Ivory
B. Tap-Coral
C. Tap-Amber
D. Tap-Slate

Directive 8: In cases where Breaker Bus-52 reported a harmonic surge, establish that Breaker Bus-52 is placed on a standby list.

A closed high-voltage substation desk enforces exact feeder rules. Use only the listed dossier records and provisions.
Closed-memo note: a status holds only if stated under Current Records, derived from Operating Directives, or supplied in a verified field update.

Current Records:
Record #1: Breaker Bus-24 is registered under active default status.
Record #2: Breaker Bus-24 belongs to Wing Primary.
Record #3: Breaker Bus-52 belongs to Wing Reserve.
Record #4: For Breaker Bus-24, the arc relay is released.
Record #5: Breaker Bus-38 passed oil dielectric test.
Record #6: Breaker Bus-11 logged grounding continuity.

Operating Directives:
Directive 1: In cases where Breaker Bus-24 reported a harmonic surge, establish that Breaker Bus-24 enters load balancing.
Directive 2: In cases where Breaker Bus-24 recorded frequency lock, establish that Breaker Bus-24 opens voltage priority.
Directive 3: In cases where Breaker Bus-24 enters load balancing and Breaker Bus-24 opens voltage priority and Breaker Bus-24 holds a dispatcher seal, establish that Breaker Bus-24 activates busbar override.
Directive 4: In cases where Breaker Bus-24 activates busbar override, replace the standing assignment and direct Breaker Bus-24 to Tap-Ivory.
Directive 5: In cases where Breaker Bus-24 reported a harmonic surge and Breaker Bus-24 enters load balancing, establish that Breaker Bus-24 carries a transformer notice.
Directive 6: In cases where Breaker Bus-24 carries a transformer notice and Breaker Bus-24 carries an emergency board waiver, replace the standing assignment and direct Breaker Bus-24 to Tap-Amber.
Directive 7: If Breaker Bus-38 passed oil dielectric test and Breaker Bus-11 logged grounding continuity, record a routine audit note for Breaker Bus-38.
Directive 8: In cases where Breaker Bus-52 reported a harmonic surge, establish that Breaker Bus-52 is placed on a standby list.

Standing Rule: Breaker Bus-24 is under active default status, so Breaker Bus-24 is assigned to Tap-Slate unless the rules establish that Breaker Bus-24 activates busbar override.

Question: Using only the current records and operating directives above, what is the assigned classification of Breaker Bus-24?
Options:
A. Tap-Coral
B. Tap-Slate
C. Tap-Ivory
D. Tap-Amber

[Case Dossier]
A closed vintner aging cellar applies exact racking rules. Use only the listed dossier records and provisions.
Closed-dossier note: an entry's status holds only when listed under Observed Statuses, derived via Decision Provisions, or reported in a verified telemetry bulletin.

Observed Statuses:
Entry 1: Cask Barrel-27 is registered under active default status.
Entry 2: Cask Barrel-27 belongs to Row Vault.
Entry 3: Cask Barrel-13 belongs to Row Crypt.
Entry 4: For Cask Barrel-27, the cork seal is released.
Entry 5: Cask Barrel-49 passed hygrometer read.
Entry 6: Cask Barrel-66 verified bung alignment.

Decision Provisions:
Clause 1 — When Cask Barrel-27 triggered an ullage check, it follows that Cask Barrel-27 enters cooper inspection.
Clause 2 — When Cask Barrel-27 logged cellar humidity clearance, it follows that Cask Barrel-27 grants vintage priority.
Clause 3 — When Cask Barrel-27 enters cooper inspection and Cask Barrel-27 grants vintage priority and Cask Barrel-27 holds a sommelier band, it follows that Cask Barrel-27 unlocks racking override.
Clause 4 — When Cask Barrel-27 unlocks racking override, supersede the baseline assignment and route Cask Barrel-27 to Rack-Quartz.
Clause 5 — When Cask Barrel-27 triggered an ullage check and Cask Barrel-27 enters cooper inspection, it follows that Cask Barrel-27 carries a stave record.
Clause 6 — When Cask Barrel-27 carries a stave record and Cask Barrel-27 carries an emergency board waiver, supersede the baseline assignment and route Cask Barrel-27 to Rack-Agate.
Clause 7 — If Cask Barrel-49 passed hygrometer read and Cask Barrel-66 verified bung alignment, record a routine audit note for Cask Barrel-49.
Clause 8 — When Cask Barrel-13 triggered an ullage check, it follows that Cask Barrel-13 is placed on a standby list.

Baseline Rule: Cask Barrel-27 is under active default status, so Cask Barrel-27 is assigned to Rack-Beryl unless the rules establish that Cask Barrel-27 unlocks racking override.

Question: Based strictly on the listed dossier entries and provisions, what is the current classification of Cask Barrel-27?
Options:
A. Rack-Quartz
B. Rack-Topaz
C. Rack-Beryl
D. Rack-Agate

[Case Dossier]
A closed high-voltage substation desk enforces exact feeder rules. Use only the listed dossier records and provisions.
Closed-dossier note: an entry's status holds only when listed under Observed Statuses, derived via Decision Provisions, or reported in a verified telemetry bulletin.

Observed Statuses:
Entry 1: Breaker Bus-52 is registered under active default status.
Entry 2: Breaker Bus-52 belongs to Wing Primary.
Entry 3: For Breaker Bus-52, the arc relay is released.
Entry 4: For Breaker Bus-38, the arc relay is engaged.
Entry 5: Breaker Bus-11 passed oil dielectric test.
Entry 6: Breaker Bus-24 logged grounding continuity.

Decision Provisions:
Clause 1 — When Breaker Bus-52 reported a harmonic surge and the arc relay is released for Breaker Bus-52, it follows that Breaker Bus-52 enters load balancing.
Clause 2 — When Breaker Bus-52 recorded frequency lock, it follows that Breaker Bus-52 opens voltage priority.
Clause 3 — When Breaker Bus-52 enters load balancing and Breaker Bus-52 opens voltage priority, it follows that Breaker Bus-52 activates busbar override.
Clause 4 — When Breaker Bus-52 activates busbar override, supersede the baseline assignment and route Breaker Bus-52 to Tap-Coral.
Clause 5 — When Breaker Bus-52 reported a harmonic surge and Breaker Bus-52 enters load balancing, it follows that Breaker Bus-52 carries a transformer notice.
Clause 6 — When Breaker Bus-52 carries a transformer notice and Breaker Bus-52 carries an emergency board waiver, supersede the baseline assignment and route Breaker Bus-52 to Tap-Ivory.
Clause 7 — If Breaker Bus-11 passed oil dielectric test and Breaker Bus-24 logged grounding continuity, record a routine audit note for Breaker Bus-11.
Clause 8 — When Breaker Bus-38 reported a harmonic surge, it follows that Breaker Bus-38 is placed on a standby list.

Baseline Rule: Breaker Bus-52 is under active default status, so Breaker Bus-52 is assigned to Tap-Amber unless the rules establish that Breaker Bus-52 activates busbar override.

Question: Based strictly on the listed dossier entries and provisions, what is the current classification of Breaker Bus-52?
Options:
A. Tap-Ivory
B. Tap-Slate
C. Tap-Amber
D. Tap-Coral

Record #1: Breaker Bus-38 is registered under active default status.
Record #2: Breaker Bus-38 belongs to Wing Reserve.
Record #3: For Breaker Bus-38, the arc relay is released.
Record #4: For Breaker Bus-24, the arc relay is engaged.
Record #5: Breaker Bus-11 passed oil dielectric test.
Record #6: Breaker Bus-52 logged grounding continuity.

Operating Directives:
Directive 1: In cases where Breaker Bus-38 reported a harmonic surge and the arc relay is released for Breaker Bus-38, establish that Breaker Bus-38 enters load balancing.

Directive 5: In cases where Breaker Bus-38 reported a harmonic surge and Breaker Bus-38 enters load balancing, establish that Breaker Bus-38 carries a transformer notice.
Directive 6: In cases where Breaker Bus-38 carries a transformer notice and Breaker Bus-38 carries an emergency board waiver, replace the standing assignment and direct Breaker Bus-38 to Tap-Ivory.
Directive 7: If Breaker Bus-11 passed oil dielectric test and Breaker Bus-52 logged grounding continuity, record a routine audit note for Breaker Bus-11.
Directive 8: In cases where Breaker Bus-24 reported a harmonic surge, establish that Breaker Bus-24 is placed on a standby list.

Standing Rule: Breaker Bus-38 is under active default status, so Breaker Bus-38 is assigned to Tap-Slate unless the rules establish that Breaker Bus-38 activates busbar override.

Question: Using only the current records and operating directives above, what is the assigned classification of Breaker Bus-38?
Options:
A. Tap-Slate
B. Tap-Amber

[Operations Memo]
A closed mountain observatory operations desk applies exact telescope dome rules. Use only the listed dossier records and provisions.
Closed-memo note: a status holds only if stated under Current Records, derived from Operating Directives, or supplied in a verified field update.

Current Records:
Record #1: Telescope Optic-47 is registered under active default status.
Record #2: Telescope Optic-47 belongs to Bay Nadir.
Record #3: Telescope Optic-68 belongs to Bay Zenith.
Record #4: Telescope Optic-29 passed collimation sweep.
Record #5: Telescope Optic-14 verified dew heater check.

Standing Rule: Telescope Optic-47 is under active default status, so Telescope Optic-47 is assigned to Dome-Lyra unless the rules establish that Telescope Optic-47 authorizes dome override.

Operating Directives:
Directive 1: In cases where Telescope Optic-47 logged a tracking shift and the shutter bolt is released for Telescope Optic-47, establish that Telescope Optic-47 enters mirror calibration.
Directive 2: In cases where Telescope Optic-47 confirmed thermal equilibrium, establish that Telescope Optic-47 clears night priority.
Directive 3: In cases where Telescope Optic-47 enters mirror calibration and Telescope Optic-47 clears night priority, establish that Telescope Optic-47 authorizes dome override.
Directive 4: In cases where Telescope Optic-47 authorizes dome override, replace the standing assignment and direct Telescope Optic-47 to Dome-Orion.
Directive 5: In cases where Telescope Optic-47 logged a tracking shift and Telescope Optic-47 enters mirror calibration, establish that Telescope Optic-47 holds a focus bulletin.
Directive 6: In cases where Telescope Optic-47 holds a focus bulletin and Telescope Optic-47 carries an emergency board waiver, replace the standing assignment and direct Telescope Optic-47 to Dome-Rigel.
Directive 7: If Telescope Optic-29 passed collimation sweep and Telescope Optic-14 verified dew heater check, record a routine audit note for Telescope Optic-29.
Directive 8: In cases where Telescope Optic-68 logged a tracking shift, establish that Telescope Optic-68 is placed on a standby list.

Question: Using only the current records and operating directives above, what is the assigned classification of Telescope Optic-47?
Options:
A. Dome-Orion
B. Dome-Rigel
C. Dome-Vega
D. Dome-Lyra

A closed high-voltage substation desk enforces exact feeder rules. Use only the listed dossier records and provisions.

Current Records:
Record #1: Breaker Bus-52 is registered under active default status.
Record #2: Breaker Bus-52 belongs to Wing Reserve.
Record #3: For Breaker Bus-52, the arc relay is released.
Record #4: For Breaker Bus-11, the arc relay is engaged.
Record #5: Breaker Bus-38 passed oil dielectric test.
Record #6: Breaker Bus-24 logged grounding continuity.

Operating Directives:
Directive 1: In cases where Breaker Bus-52 reported a harmonic surge, establish that Breaker Bus-52 enters load balancing.
Directive 2: In cases where Breaker Bus-52 recorded frequency lock and the arc relay is released for Breaker Bus-52, establish that Breaker Bus-52 opens voltage priority.
Directive 3: In cases where Breaker Bus-52 enters load balancing and Breaker Bus-52 opens voltage priority, establish that Breaker Bus-52 activates busbar override.
Directive 4: In cases where Breaker Bus-52 activates busbar override, replace the standing assignment and direct Breaker Bus-52 to Tap-Ivory.
Directive 5: In cases where Breaker Bus-52 reported a harmonic surge and Breaker Bus-52 enters load balancing, establish that Breaker Bus-52 carries a transformer notice.
Directive 6: In cases where Breaker Bus-52 carries a transformer notice and Breaker Bus-52 carries an emergency board waiver, replace the standing assignment and direct Breaker Bus-52 to Tap-Coral.
Directive 7: If Breaker Bus-38 passed oil dielectric test and Breaker Bus-24 logged grounding continuity, record a routine audit note for Breaker Bus-38.
Directive 8: In cases where Breaker Bus-11 reported a harmonic surge, establish that Breaker Bus-11 is placed on a standby list.

Standing Rule: Breaker Bus-52 is under active default status, so Breaker Bus-52 is assigned to Tap-Slate unless the rules establish that Breaker Bus-52 activates busbar override.

Question: Using only the current records and operating directives above, what is the assigned classification of Breaker Bus-52?
Options:
A. Tap-Amber
B. Tap-Ivory
C. Tap-Slate
D. Tap-Coral

Directive 8: In cases where Breaker Bus-38 reported a harmonic surge, establish that Breaker Bus-38 is placed on a standby list.

Question: Using only the current records and operating directives above, what is the assigned classification of Breaker Bus-52?

Entry 5: Beacon Float-21 cleared solar panel check.
Entry 6: Beacon Float-43 logged transponder sync.

Clause 1 — When Beacon Float-85 sent a drift beacon, it follows that Beacon Float-85 enters sonar validation.

Clause 5 — When Beacon Float-85 sent a drift beacon and Beacon Float-85 enters sonar validation, it follows that Beacon Float-85 holds a current digest.

Clause 7 — If Beacon Float-21 cleared solar panel check and Beacon Float-43 logged transponder sync, record a routine audit note for Beacon Float-21.
Clause 8 — When Beacon Float-64 sent a drift beacon, it follows that Beacon Float-64 is placed on a standby list.

Baseline Rule: Beacon Float-85 is under active default status, so Beacon Float-85 is assigned to Channel-Plover unless the rules establish that Beacon Float-85 authorizes mooring override.

context_prompt_v:
[Operations Memo]
A closed high-voltage substation desk enforces exact feeder rules. Use only the listed dossier records and provisions.
Closed-memo note: a status holds only if stated under Current Records, derived from Operating Directives, or supplied in a verified field update.

Current Records:
Record #1: Breaker Bus-38 is registered under active default status.
Record #2: Breaker Bus-38 belongs to Wing Reserve.
Record #3: For Breaker Bus-38, the arc relay is released.
Record #4: For Breaker Bus-24, the arc relay is engaged.
Record #5: Breaker Bus-52 passed oil dielectric test.
Record #6: Breaker Bus-11 logged grounding continuity.

Operating Directives:
Directive 1: In cases where Breaker Bus-38 reported a harmonic surge, establish that Breaker Bus-38 enters load balancing.
Directive 2: In cases where Breaker Bus-38 recorded frequency lock, establish that Breaker Bus-38 opens voltage priority.
Directive 3: In cases where Breaker Bus-38 enters load balancing and Breaker Bus-38 opens voltage priority and the arc relay is released for Breaker Bus-38, establish that Breaker Bus-38 activates busbar override.
Directive 4: In cases where Breaker Bus-38 activates busbar override, replace the standing assignment and direct Breaker Bus-38 to Tap-Slate.
Directive 5: In cases where Breaker Bus-38 reported a harmonic surge and Breaker Bus-38 enters load balancing, establish that Breaker Bus-38 carries a transformer notice.
Directive 6: In cases where Breaker Bus-38 carries a transformer notice and Breaker Bus-38 carries an emergency board waiver, replace the standing assignment and direct Breaker Bus-38 to Tap-Ivory.
Directive 7: If Breaker Bus-52 passed oil dielectric test and Breaker Bus-11 logged grounding continuity, record a routine audit note for Breaker Bus-52.
Directive 8: In cases where Breaker Bus-24 reported a harmonic surge, establish that Breaker Bus-24 is placed on a standby list.

Standing Rule: Breaker Bus-38 is under active default status, so Breaker Bus-38 is assigned to Tap-Amber unless the rules establish that Breaker Bus-38 activates busbar override.

Question: Using only the current records and operating directives above, what is the assigned classification of Breaker Bus-38?
Options:
A. Tap-Coral
B. Tap-Amber
C. Tap-Slate
D. Tap-Ivory

Clause 8 — When Sensor Node-17 emitted a p-wave chime, it follows that Sensor Node-17 is placed on a standby list.

A closed high-voltage substation desk enforces exact feeder rules. Use only the listed dossier records and provisions.

Current Records:
Record #1: Breaker Bus-11 is registered under active default status.
Record #2: Breaker Bus-11 belongs to Wing Reserve.
Record #3: For Breaker Bus-11, the arc relay is released.
Record #4: Breaker Bus-24 passed oil dielectric test.
Record #5: Breaker Bus-38 logged grounding continuity.

Standing Rule: Breaker Bus-11 is under active default status, so Breaker Bus-11 is assigned to Tap-Coral unless the rules establish that Breaker Bus-11 activates busbar override.

Directive 1: In cases where Breaker Bus-11 reported a harmonic surge and the phase drift is at least 25, establish that Breaker Bus-11 enters load balancing.
Directive 2: In cases where Breaker Bus-11 recorded frequency lock, establish that Breaker Bus-11 opens voltage priority.

Directive 4: In cases where Breaker Bus-11 activates busbar override, replace the standing assignment and direct Breaker Bus-11 to Tap-Slate.
Directive 5: In cases where Breaker Bus-11 reported a harmonic surge and Breaker Bus-11 enters load balancing, establish that Breaker Bus-11 carries a transformer notice.
Directive 6: In cases where Breaker Bus-11 carries a transformer notice and Breaker Bus-11 carries an emergency board waiver, replace the standing assignment and direct Breaker Bus-11 to Tap-Ivory.
Directive 7: If Breaker Bus-24 passed oil dielectric test and Breaker Bus-38 logged grounding continuity, record a routine audit note for Breaker Bus-24.
Directive 8: In cases where Breaker Bus-52 reported a harmonic surge, establish that Breaker Bus-52 is placed on a standby list.

Question: Using only the current records and operating directives above, what is the assigned classification of Breaker Bus-11?
Options:
A. Tap-Amber
B. Tap-Slate
C. Tap-Ivory
D. Tap-Coral

Directive 8: In cases where Breaker Bus-38 reported a harmonic surge, establish that Breaker Bus-38 is placed on a standby list.

Question: Using only the current records and operating directives above, what is the assigned classification of Breaker Bus-52?

Closed-dossier note: an entry's status holds only when listed under Observed Statuses, derived via Decision Provisions, or reported in a verified telemetry bulletin.

Observed Statuses:
Entry 1: Breaker Bus-24 is registered under active default status.
Entry 2: Breaker Bus-24 belongs to Wing Reserve.
Entry 3: For Breaker Bus-24, the arc relay is released.
Entry 4: Breaker Bus-11 passed oil dielectric test.
Entry 5: Breaker Bus-38 logged grounding continuity.

Baseline Rule: Breaker Bus-24 is under active default status, so Breaker Bus-24 is assigned to Tap-Coral unless the rules establish that Breaker Bus-24 activates busbar override.

Clause 1 — When Breaker Bus-24 reported a harmonic surge and the phase drift is at least 50, it follows that Breaker Bus-24 enters load balancing.
Clause 2 — When Breaker Bus-24 recorded frequency lock, it follows that Breaker Bus-24 opens voltage priority.
Clause 3 — When Breaker Bus-24 enters load balancing and Breaker Bus-24 opens voltage priority, it follows that Breaker Bus-24 activates busbar override.
Clause 4 — When Breaker Bus-24 activates busbar override, supersede the baseline assignment and route Breaker Bus-24 to Tap-Slate.
Clause 5 — When Breaker Bus-24 reported a harmonic surge and Breaker Bus-24 enters load balancing, it follows that Breaker Bus-24 carries a transformer notice.

A closed geothermal seismic monitoring station applies exact telemetry rules. Use only the listed dossier records and provisions.
Closed-dossier note: an entry's status holds only when listed under Observed Statuses, derived via Decision Provisions, or reported in a verified telemetry bulletin.

Observed Statuses:
Entry 1: Sensor Node-35 is registered under active default status.
Entry 2: Sensor Node-35 belongs to Ridge Trough.
Entry 3: For Sensor Node-35, the tremor gate is released.
Entry 4: Sensor Node-78 passed geophone ping.
Entry 5: Sensor Node-53 verified battery voltage.

Decision Provisions:
Clause 1 — When Sensor Node-35 emitted a p-wave chime, it follows that Sensor Node-35 enters waveform triage.
Clause 2 — When Sensor Node-35 confirmed borehole telemetry sync and the shear count is at least 25, it follows that Sensor Node-35 enables array priority.
Clause 3 — When Sensor Node-35 enters waveform triage and Sensor Node-35 enables array priority, it follows that Sensor Node-35 triggers borehole override.
Clause 4 — When Sensor Node-35 triggers borehole override, supersede the baseline assignment and route Sensor Node-35 to Band-Pulse.
Clause 5 — When Sensor Node-35 emitted a p-wave chime and Sensor Node-35 enters waveform triage, it follows that Sensor Node-35 carries a spectrum log.
Clause 6 — When Sensor Node-35 carries a spectrum log and Sensor Node-35 carries an emergency board waiver, supersede the baseline assignment and route Sensor Node-35 to Band-Echo.
Clause 7 — If Sensor Node-78 passed geophone ping and Sensor Node-53 verified battery voltage, record a routine audit note for Sensor Node-78.
Clause 8 — When Sensor Node-17 emitted a p-wave chime, it follows that Sensor Node-17 is placed on a standby list.

Baseline Rule: Sensor Node-35 is under active default status, so Sensor Node-35 is assigned to Band-Drift unless the rules establish that Sensor Node-35 triggers borehole override.

Question: Based strictly on the listed dossier entries and provisions, what is the current classification of Sensor Node-35?
Options:
A. Band-Wave
B. Band-Echo
C. Band-Pulse
D. Band-Drift

Directive 8: In cases where Sensor Node-35 emitted a p-wave chime, establish that Sensor Node-35 is placed on a standby list.

Standing Rule: Sensor Node-53 is under active default status, so Sensor Node-53 is assigned to Band-Pulse unless the rules establish that Sensor Node-53 triggers borehole override.

Question: Using only the current records and operating directives above, what is the assigned classification of Sensor Node-53?

Directive 7: If Beacon Float-21 cleared solar panel check and Beacon Float-85 logged transponder sync, record a routine audit note for Beacon Float-21.
Directive 8: In cases where Beacon Float-64 sent a drift beacon, establish that Beacon Float-64 is placed on a standby list.

Question: Using only the current records and operating directives above, what is the assigned classification of Beacon Float-43?

B. Channel-Plover

Record #1: Breaker Bus-52 is registered under active default status.
Record #2: For Breaker Bus-52, the arc relay is released.
Record #3: Breaker Bus-24 belongs to Wing Reserve.
Record #4: Breaker Bus-11 passed oil dielectric test.
Record #5: Breaker Bus-38 logged grounding continuity.

Standing Rule: Breaker Bus-52 is under active default status, so Breaker Bus-52 is assigned to Tap-Slate unless the rules establish that Breaker Bus-52 activates busbar override.

Directive 4: In cases where Breaker Bus-52 activates busbar override, replace the standing assignment and direct Breaker Bus-52 to Tap-Amber.
Directive 5: In cases where Breaker Bus-52 reported a harmonic surge and Breaker Bus-52 enters load balancing, establish that Breaker Bus-52 carries a transformer notice.
Directive 6: In cases where Breaker Bus-52 carries a transformer notice and Breaker Bus-52 carries an emergency board waiver, replace the standing assignment and direct Breaker Bus-52 to Tap-Ivory.
Directive 7: If Breaker Bus-11 passed oil dielectric test and Breaker Bus-38 logged grounding continuity, record a routine audit note for Breaker Bus-11.
Directive 8: In cases where Breaker Bus-24 reported a harmonic surge, establish that Breaker Bus-24 is placed on a standby list.

Question: Using only the current records and operating directives above, what is the assigned classification of Breaker Bus-52?
Options:
A. Tap-Amber
B. Tap-Slate
C. Tap-Ivory
D. Tap-Coral

Entry 6: Breaker Bus-11 logged grounding continuity.

Clause 6 — When Breaker Bus-52 carries a transformer notice and Breaker Bus-52 carries an emergency board waiver, supersede the baseline assignment and route Breaker Bus-52 to Tap-Slate.
Clause 7 — If Breaker Bus-24 passed oil dielectric test and Breaker Bus-11 logged grounding continuity, record a routine audit note for Breaker Bus-24.
Clause 8 — When Breaker Bus-38 reported a harmonic surge, it follows that Breaker Bus-38 is placed on a standby list.

[Operations Memo]
A closed geothermal seismic monitoring station applies exact telemetry rules. Use only the listed dossier records and provisions.
Closed-memo note: a status holds only if stated under Current Records, derived from Operating Directives, or supplied in a verified field update.

Current Records:
Record #1: Sensor Node-35 is registered under active default status.
Record #2: Sensor Node-35 belongs to Ridge Trough.
Record #3: Sensor Node-53 belongs to Ridge Crest.
Record #4: Sensor Node-17 passed geophone ping.
Record #5: Sensor Node-78 verified battery voltage.

Standing Rule: Sensor Node-35 is under active default status, so Sensor Node-35 is assigned to Band-Wave unless the rules establish that Sensor Node-35 triggers borehole override.

Operating Directives:
Directive 1: In cases where Sensor Node-35 emitted a p-wave chime and the tremor gate is released for Sensor Node-35, establish that Sensor Node-35 enters waveform triage.
Directive 2: In cases where Sensor Node-35 confirmed borehole telemetry sync, establish that Sensor Node-35 enables array priority.
Directive 3: In cases where Sensor Node-35 enters waveform triage and Sensor Node-35 enables array priority, establish that Sensor Node-35 triggers borehole override.
Directive 4: In cases where Sensor Node-35 triggers borehole override, replace the standing assignment and direct Sensor Node-35 to Band-Echo.
Directive 5: In cases where Sensor Node-35 emitted a p-wave chime and Sensor Node-35 enters waveform triage, establish that Sensor Node-35 carries a spectrum log.
Directive 6: In cases where Sensor Node-35 carries a spectrum log and Sensor Node-35 carries an emergency board waiver, replace the standing assignment and direct Sensor Node-35 to Band-Drift.
Directive 7: If Sensor Node-17 passed geophone ping and Sensor Node-78 verified battery voltage, record a routine audit note for Sensor Node-17.
Directive 8: In cases where Sensor Node-53 emitted a p-wave chime, establish that Sensor Node-53 is placed on a standby list.

Question: Using only the current records and operating directives above, what is the assigned classification of Sensor Node-35?
Options:
A. Band-Wave
B. Band-Drift
C. Band-Pulse
D. Band-Echo

A closed geothermal seismic monitoring station applies exact telemetry rules. Use only the listed dossier records and provisions.
Closed-dossier note: an entry's status holds only when listed under Observed Statuses, derived via Decision Provisions, or reported in a verified telemetry bulletin.

Observed Statuses:
Entry 1: Sensor Node-35 is registered under active default status.
Entry 2: Sensor Node-35 belongs to Ridge Crest.
Entry 3: For Sensor Node-35, the tremor gate is released.
Entry 4: For Sensor Node-17, the tremor gate is engaged.
Entry 5: Sensor Node-78 passed geophone ping.
Entry 6: Sensor Node-53 verified battery voltage.

Baseline Rule: Sensor Node-35 is under active default status, so Sensor Node-35 is assigned to Band-Echo unless the rules establish that Sensor Node-35 triggers borehole override.

Decision Provisions:
Clause 1 — When Sensor Node-35 emitted a p-wave chime, it follows that Sensor Node-35 enters waveform triage.
Clause 2 — When Sensor Node-35 confirmed borehole telemetry sync, it follows that Sensor Node-35 enables array priority.
Clause 3 — When Sensor Node-35 enters waveform triage and Sensor Node-35 enables array priority and the tremor gate is released for Sensor Node-35, it follows that Sensor Node-35 triggers borehole override.
Clause 4 — When Sensor Node-35 triggers borehole override, supersede the baseline assignment and route Sensor Node-35 to Band-Drift.
Clause 5 — When Sensor Node-35 emitted a p-wave chime and Sensor Node-35 enters waveform triage, it follows that Sensor Node-35 carries a spectrum log.
Clause 6 — When Sensor Node-35 carries a spectrum log and Sensor Node-35 carries an emergency board waiver, supersede the baseline assignment and route Sensor Node-35 to Band-Pulse.
Clause 7 — If Sensor Node-78 passed geophone ping and Sensor Node-53 verified battery voltage, record a routine audit note for Sensor Node-78.
Clause 8 — When Sensor Node-17 emitted a p-wave chime, it follows that Sensor Node-17 is placed on a standby list.

Question: Based strictly on the listed dossier entries and provisions, what is the current classification of Sensor Node-35?
Options:
A. Band-Wave
B. Band-Echo
C. Band-Pulse
D. Band-Drift

Directive 8: In cases where Telescope Optic-47 logged a tracking shift, establish that Telescope Optic-47 is placed on a standby list.

Question: Using only the current records and operating directives above, what is the assigned classification of Telescope Optic-29?

[Operations Memo]
A closed high-voltage substation desk enforces exact feeder rules. Use only the listed dossier records and provisions.
Closed-memo note: a status holds only if stated under Current Records, derived from Operating Directives, or supplied in a verified field update.

Current Records:
Record #1: Breaker Bus-52 is registered under active default status.
Record #2: Breaker Bus-52 belongs to Wing Primary.
Record #3: For Breaker Bus-52, the arc relay is released.
Record #4: Breaker Bus-11 passed oil dielectric test.
Record #5: Breaker Bus-24 logged grounding continuity.

Standing Rule: Breaker Bus-52 is under active default status, so Breaker Bus-52 is assigned to Tap-Ivory unless the rules establish that Breaker Bus-52 activates busbar override.

Operating Directives:
Directive 1: In cases where Breaker Bus-52 reported a harmonic surge and the phase drift is at least 74, establish that Breaker Bus-52 enters load balancing.
Directive 2: In cases where Breaker Bus-52 recorded frequency lock, establish that Breaker Bus-52 opens voltage priority.
Directive 3: In cases where Breaker Bus-52 enters load balancing and Breaker Bus-52 opens voltage priority, establish that Breaker Bus-52 activates busbar override.
Directive 4: In cases where Breaker Bus-52 activates busbar override, replace the standing assignment and direct Breaker Bus-52 to Tap-Amber.
Directive 5: In cases where Breaker Bus-52 reported a harmonic surge and Breaker Bus-52 enters load balancing, establish that Breaker Bus-52 carries a transformer notice.
Directive 6: In cases where Breaker Bus-52 carries a transformer notice and Breaker Bus-52 carries an emergency board waiver, replace the standing assignment and direct Breaker Bus-52 to Tap-Slate.
Directive 7: If Breaker Bus-11 passed oil dielectric test and Breaker Bus-24 logged grounding continuity, record a routine audit note for Breaker Bus-11.
Directive 8: In cases where Breaker Bus-38 reported a harmonic surge, establish that Breaker Bus-38 is placed on a standby list.

Question: Using only the current records and operating directives above, what is the assigned classification of Breaker Bus-52?
Options:
A. Tap-Coral
B. Tap-Slate
C. Tap-Amber
D. Tap-Ivory

Directive 7: In cases where Beacon Float-85 enables buoy priority, establish that Beacon Float-85 receives a periodic log review.
Directive 8: For entries in Tide Outer, if Beacon Float-85 sent a drift beacon, then Beacon Float-85 is queued for archival.

Based only on the current records and operating directives, what is the assigned classification for Beacon Float-85?

Directive 8: For entries in Tide Inner, if Beacon Float-64 sent a drift beacon, then Beacon Float-64 is queued for archival.

Directive 9: In cases where an entry holds a current digest and carries an emergency board waiver, replace the standing assignment and direct it to Channel-Kestrel.

Clause 7 — When Barge Sluice-31 approves passage priority, it follows that Barge Sluice-31 receives a periodic log review.
Clause 8 — For entries in Basin High, if Barge Sluice-31 signaled a keel trim, then Barge Sluice-31 is queued for archival.

Based only on the listed dossier entries and provisions, what is the assigned classification for Barge Sluice-31?
A) Berth-Cedar
B) Berth-Larch
C) Berth-Maple

Clause 6 — When Telescope Optic-68 logged a tracking shift, it follows that Telescope Optic-68 is placed on a watch list.
Clause 7 — When Telescope Optic-14 clears night priority, it follows that Telescope Optic-14 receives a periodic log review.
Clause 8 — For entries in Bay Nadir, if Telescope Optic-14 logged a tracking shift, then Telescope Optic-14 is queued for archival.

Clause 9 — When an entry holds a focus bulletin and carries an emergency board waiver, supersede the baseline assignment and route it to Dome-Rigel.
Based only on the listed dossier entries and provisions, what is the assigned classification for Telescope Optic-14?
A) Dome-Orion
B) Dome-Rigel

context_prompt_v:
[Operations Memo]
A closed mountain observatory operations desk applies exact telescope dome rules. Use only the listed dossier records and provisions.
Closed-memo note: a status holds only if stated under Current Records, derived from Operating Directives, or supplied in a verified field update.

Current Records:
Record #1: Telescope Optic-68 is registered under active default status.
Record #2: Telescope Optic-68 belongs to Bay Nadir.
Record #3: For Telescope Optic-68, the shutter bolt is released.
Record #4: Telescope Optic-29 passed collimation sweep.
Record #5: Telescope Optic-14 verified dew heater check.

Standing Rule: Telescope Optic-68 is under active default status, so Telescope Optic-68 is assigned to Dome-Vega unless the rules establish that Telescope Optic-68 authorizes dome override.

Operating Directives:
Directive 1: In cases where Telescope Optic-68 logged a tracking shift, establish that Telescope Optic-68 clears night priority.
Directive 2: In cases where Telescope Optic-68 clears night priority, establish that Telescope Optic-68 holds a focus bulletin.
Directive 3: In cases where Telescope Optic-68 holds a focus bulletin, establish that Telescope Optic-68 authorizes dome override.
Directive 4: In cases where Telescope Optic-68 authorizes dome override, replace the standing assignment and direct Telescope Optic-68 to Dome-Rigel.
Directive 5: If Telescope Optic-29 passed collimation sweep and Telescope Optic-14 verified dew heater check, record a routine audit note for Telescope Optic-29.
Directive 6: In cases where Telescope Optic-47 logged a tracking shift, establish that Telescope Optic-47 is placed on a watch list.
Directive 7: In cases where Telescope Optic-68 clears night priority, establish that Telescope Optic-68 receives a periodic log review.
Directive 8: For entries in Bay Zenith, if Telescope Optic-68 logged a tracking shift, then Telescope Optic-68 is queued for archival.

Directive 9: In cases where an entry holds a focus bulletin and carries an emergency board waiver, replace the standing assignment and direct it to Dome-Lyra.
Based only on the current records and operating directives, what is the assigned classification for Telescope Optic-68?
A) Dome-Rigel
B) Dome-Orion
C) Dome-Lyra
D) Dome-Vega

[Case Dossier]
A closed geothermal seismic monitoring station applies exact telemetry rules. Use only the listed dossier records and provisions.
Closed-dossier note: an entry's status holds only when listed under Observed Statuses, derived via Decision Provisions, or reported in a verified telemetry bulletin.

Observed Statuses:
Entry 1: Sensor Node-53 is registered under active default status.
Entry 2: Sensor Node-53 belongs to Ridge Crest.
Entry 3: For Sensor Node-53, the tremor gate is released.
Entry 4: Sensor Node-17 passed geophone ping.
Entry 5: Sensor Node-78 verified battery voltage.

Baseline Rule: Sensor Node-53 is under active default status, so Sensor Node-53 is assigned to Band-Drift unless the rules establish that Sensor Node-53 triggers borehole override.

Decision Provisions:
Clause 1 — When Sensor Node-53 emitted a p-wave chime, it follows that Sensor Node-53 enables array priority.
Clause 2 — When Sensor Node-53 enables array priority, it follows that Sensor Node-53 carries a spectrum log.
Clause 3 — When Sensor Node-53 carries a spectrum log, it follows that Sensor Node-53 triggers borehole override.
Clause 4 — When Sensor Node-53 triggers borehole override, supersede the baseline assignment and route Sensor Node-53 to Band-Wave.
Clause 5 — If Sensor Node-17 passed geophone ping and Sensor Node-78 verified battery voltage, record a routine audit note for Sensor Node-17.
Clause 6 — When Sensor Node-35 emitted a p-wave chime, it follows that Sensor Node-35 is placed on a watch list.
Clause 7 — When Sensor Node-53 enables array priority, it follows that Sensor Node-53 receives a periodic log review.
Clause 8 — For entries in Ridge Trough, if Sensor Node-53 emitted a p-wave chime, then Sensor Node-53 is queued for archival.

Clause 9 — When an entry carries a spectrum log and carries an emergency board waiver, supersede the baseline assignment and route it to Band-Pulse.
Based only on the listed dossier entries and provisions, what is the assigned classification for Sensor Node-53?
A) Band-Echo
B) Band-Pulse
C) Band-Drift
D) Band-Wave

Record #2: Telescope Optic-47 belongs to Bay Zenith.

Directive 7: In cases where Telescope Optic-47 clears night priority, establish that Telescope Optic-47 receives a periodic log review.
Directive 8: For entries in Bay Nadir, if Telescope Optic-47 logged a tracking shift, then Telescope Optic-47 is queued for archival.

Based only on the current records and operating directives, what is the assigned classification for Telescope Optic-47?
A) Dome-Rigel

Observed Statuses:
Entry 1: Breaker Bus-11 is registered under active default status.
Entry 2: Breaker Bus-11 belongs to Wing Primary.
Entry 3: For Breaker Bus-11, the arc relay is released.
Entry 4: Breaker Bus-24 passed oil dielectric test.
Entry 5: Breaker Bus-38 logged grounding continuity.

Decision Provisions:
Clause 1 — When Breaker Bus-11 reported a harmonic surge, it follows that Breaker Bus-11 opens voltage priority.
Clause 2 — When Breaker Bus-11 opens voltage priority, it follows that Breaker Bus-11 carries a transformer notice.

Clause 4 — When Breaker Bus-11 activates busbar override, supersede the baseline assignment and route Breaker Bus-11 to Tap-Amber.
Clause 5 — If Breaker Bus-24 passed oil dielectric test and Breaker Bus-38 logged grounding continuity, record a routine audit note for Breaker Bus-24.
Clause 6 — When Breaker Bus-52 reported a harmonic surge, it follows that Breaker Bus-52 is placed on a watch list.
Clause 7 — When Breaker Bus-11 opens voltage priority, it follows that Breaker Bus-11 receives a periodic log review.
Clause 8 — For entries in Wing Reserve, if Breaker Bus-11 reported a harmonic surge, then Breaker Bus-11 is queued for archival.

Clause 9 — When an entry carries a transformer notice and carries an emergency board waiver, supersede the baseline assignment and route it to Tap-Coral.
Baseline Rule: Breaker Bus-11 is under active default status, so Breaker Bus-11 is assigned to Tap-Ivory unless the rules establish that Breaker Bus-11 activates busbar override.

Based only on the listed dossier entries and provisions, what is the assigned classification for Breaker Bus-11?
A) Tap-Ivory
B) Tap-Amber

D) Tap-Slate

context_prompt_v:
[Case Dossier]
A closed mountain observatory operations desk applies exact telescope dome rules. Use only the listed dossier records and provisions.
Closed-dossier note: an entry's status holds only when listed under Observed Statuses, derived via Decision Provisions, or reported in a verified telemetry bulletin.

Observed Statuses:
Entry 1: Telescope Optic-47 is registered under active default status.
Entry 2: Telescope Optic-47 belongs to Bay Nadir.
Entry 3: For Telescope Optic-47, the shutter bolt is released.
Entry 4: Telescope Optic-14 passed collimation sweep.
Entry 5: Telescope Optic-68 verified dew heater check.

Baseline Rule: Telescope Optic-47 is under active default status, so Telescope Optic-47 is assigned to Dome-Vega unless the rules establish that Telescope Optic-47 authorizes dome override.

Decision Provisions:
Clause 1 — When Telescope Optic-29 logged a tracking shift, it follows that Telescope Optic-47 clears night priority.
Clause 2 — When Telescope Optic-47 clears night priority, it follows that Telescope Optic-47 holds a focus bulletin.
Clause 3 — When Telescope Optic-47 holds a focus bulletin, it follows that Telescope Optic-47 authorizes dome override.
Clause 4 — When Telescope Optic-47 authorizes dome override, supersede the baseline assignment and route Telescope Optic-47 to Dome-Lyra.
Clause 5 — If Telescope Optic-14 passed collimation sweep and Telescope Optic-68 verified dew heater check, record a routine audit note for Telescope Optic-14.
Clause 6 — When Telescope Optic-29 logged a tracking shift, it follows that Telescope Optic-29 is placed on a watch list.
Clause 7 — When Telescope Optic-47 clears night priority, it follows that Telescope Optic-47 receives a periodic log review.
Clause 8 — For entries in Bay Zenith, if Telescope Optic-47 logged a tracking shift, then Telescope Optic-47 is queued for archival.

Clause 9 — When an entry holds a focus bulletin and carries an emergency board waiver, supersede the baseline assignment and route it to Dome-Rigel.
Based only on the listed dossier entries and provisions, what is the assigned classification for Telescope Optic-47?
A) Dome-Lyra
B) Dome-Rigel
C) Dome-Vega
D) Dome-Orion
